card.text: The dwarf planet in the asteroid belt, mapped by Dawn.

introduction.text: Ceres is the largest body in the asteroid belt. Dawn found bright salt deposits across its cratered surface.

normal.title: FC visible-light mosaic
normal.summary: Dawn's visible-light mosaic, with photographed shadows; some dark edges are uncertain.

enhanced.title: False-color mosaic PIA19977
enhanced.summary: False colors from the 920, 750 and 440 nm bands, with photographed shadows.

elevation.title: HAMO digital terrain model
elevation.summary: Height above or below a 470 km sphere. Terrain beyond 60° latitude is withheld.

clay-band.title: Dawn VIR 2.7 µm band depth
clay-band.summary: Clay-bearing minerals absorb infrared light near 2.7 µm; deeper absorption means a stronger signal, not a clay percentage.

ammonium-band.title: Dawn VIR 3.1 µm band depth
ammonium-band.summary: Ammonium contains nitrogen and hydrogen; absorption near 3.1 µm traces it in surface minerals.

clay-centre.title: Dawn VIR 2.7 µm band centre
clay-centre.summary: Wavelength of clay absorption, nearly uniform across Ceres. Scan artifacts remain; poles are unmeasured.

ammonium-centre.title: Dawn VIR 3.1 µm band centre
ammonium-centre.summary: Position of the ammonium absorption, not its depth or abundance. Archive striping remains; poles are unmeasured.
